title: Working with Framework Tooling
learning_outcomes: Explain what working with framework tooling contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: framework cli commands.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. In this lesson, focus on framework cli commands; then compare it with configuration conventions. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use working with framework tooling when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. For working with framework tooling, begin with framework cli commands. Also distinguish configuration conventions; debugging facilities; migration and testing tools. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Working with Framework Tooling

$required = ["status", "message"]; $response = ["status" => 200, "message" => "ok"];
echo count(array_intersect($required, array_keys($response))) . " fields matched" . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
